output.title: Privacy promises do not control your workflow
output.body:
If you are evaluating AI for a small business, privacy promises are only part of the picture. A vendor can tell you where data is stored, how it is protected, and what terms apply. That still does not answer the more practical question: who can do what once the data enters your workflow.

That is the control decision I would make first. For any repeatable process, such as invoice handling or customer replies, decide whether the AI is allowed to act on its own or only recommend an action and wait for human approval. For money movement and other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory. That is Bareni policy, not a suggestion.

A privacy policy does not replace your own approval rules. If the workflow is loose, a careful vendor will not fix that for you. If the workflow is tight, you can use AI without handing over the keys to the shop.

One simple diagnostic question: will I see the input, the reasoning, and the recommended action before anything is committed?

The next step is to map your most repeated workflow, mark the points where money, customer communication, or data deletion could happen, and define which of those stages must stay human-approved.
